name: Navigation Tour
description: A brief tutorial covering the simulator's essential features.

steps.title: Welcome to RVCAT-WEB!
steps.description:
This tutorial will show you the different parts of the web-application.
Let's start with the program description

steps.title: Program description
steps.description:
The simulated program consists of a fixed-iteration loop of machine instructions,
described in high-level informal language, where N = total iterations (user-configurable).
For each instruction, you can view (type button):
(1) type and operand sizes;
(2) latency and eligible execution ports;
(3) input/output operands;
(4) memory addresses, strides, and vector lanes used.

The simulation models data dependencies but does not model processor registers,
memory states, branch outcomes, or memory dependencies (e.g., store-load orderings).

steps.title: Processor description
steps.description:
A table summarizes the processor pipeline's microarchitecture:
(1) Dispatch width – max instructions issued to the Execution Engine per cycle;
(2) Scheduling policy – greedy (oldest ready instructions first) or optimal (best combination);
(3) Execution ports (P0–Px) – each handles one instruction per cycle from a specific subset of types;
(4) ROB size – max instructions in the Execution Engine;
(5) Cache config – blocks, block size, miss penalty, and issue time;
(6) Retire width – max instructions retired from the Execution Engine per cycle.

steps.title: Simulation Results
steps.description:
Run simulations of your code to obtain
· global performance metrics,
· usage percentage of main elements of execution engine,
· and breakdown of critical execution path.

steps.title: Timeline
steps.description:
The Execution Timeline maps out-of-order instruction execution cycle by cycle,
while state symbols track their progress—from Dispatch (D) to Retire (R).
This view clearly highlights data dependencies, execution port stalls,
and the red critical path dictating overall execution time.

steps.title: Static Analysis
steps.description:
The Static Performance Analysis panel calculates
theoretical execution limits in advance of full simulation.
It identifies potential throughput and latency bottlenecks
by evaluating processor port constraints alongside
recurring data dependence graphs,
determining whether hardware resource bounds or
cyclic dependencies dictate overall execution speed.

steps.title: Tutorial Editor
steps.description: Create or modify your own tutorials (even this tutorial)

steps.title: Tutorial Complete!
steps.description:
Navigation tour completed!
Click the Run Simulation button to execute the loop
and explore the performance results.
Hover your cursor over metrics and timeline states
to reveal interactive tooltips with detailed execution insights.
